title: Resources
intro: What the hundred games are built with, what we reach for next, and where to look if you want to see how.

items.name: Build Ledger
items.note: Every project, measured from its own git history. Days, commits, lines, what is live.

items.name: Relay
items.note: The house template for daily link-first games. Two files of game, everything else built in.

items.name: Silly Ninjas art
items.note: Every sheet in the Silly Ninjas kit: the five ninjas with their poses and emotes, and ten worlds of props, ground and cast. Shared by Silly Ninja Defense and Silly Ninja Squares.

items.name: The tray
items.note: One script tag gives any game EJECT and SUBSCRIBE. It renders in a shadow root so it looks the same in every codebase and touches none of them.

items.name: The pad
items.note: One script tag and a PlayStation controller plays a game that was written for a mouse. It sends arrow keys, falls back to WASD, then to walking the buttons on screen, then to a drawn cursor that clicks — whichever the game turns out to want.

items.name: Dan Viau
items.note: Built tally, the analytics in every game, and the Zen redesign of Hex Smash that became the house look. Also the arcade hub and Hex Smash Ninja.

items.name: Gustavo Konrad
items.note: Rebuilt Lore Wars and BREACH on Solid, and built Wizard Battle and Overland.

items.name: Claude Code
items.note: Every game on the shelf was built with it.

items.name: Railway
items.note: Where the games are hosted.

items.name: Neon
items.note: Postgres for the games that keep state.

items.name: Midjourney
items.note: The cartridge photographs, and most of the game art.

items.name: three.js
items.note: The 3D games: crowds, apartment towers, zombies.

items.name: Porkbun
items.note: Domains.

items.name: PixiJS
items.note: Fast 2D rendering on WebGL and WebGPU. The hex games draw with it.

items.name: Phaser
items.note: A full 2D game framework with scenes, physics, input and loaders, for games that outgrow a canvas and a loop.

items.name: KAPLAY
items.note: A small, friendly 2D library for prototypes that need to be playable in an hour.

items.name: Rapier
items.note: Deterministic 2D and 3D physics compiled to WebAssembly, so a replay on the server lands the same as the phone.

items.name: Matter.js
items.note: Plain JavaScript 2D rigid bodies, for stacking, toppling and anything that needs to wobble.

items.name: GSAP
items.note: Tweening and timelines, now free. The easy way to make a win moment land.

items.name: howler.js
items.note: Audio sprites and playback that works the same on every phone browser.

items.name: Tone.js
items.note: Synths and scheduling on the Web Audio clock, for music that follows the game.

items.name: ZzFX
items.note: A sound effect is one line of numbers. No files to load.

items.name: boardgame.io
items.note: Turn-based state, moves and multiplayer sync, for games people play across a whole day.

items.name: Colyseus
items.note: Authoritative rooms for real-time multiplayer, with state synced to every seat.

items.name: PartyKit
items.note: A room per group chat on Cloudflare, for live shared boards without running a server.

items.name: rot.js
items.note: Roguelike toolkit: field of view, pathfinding, map generators and a seeded random.

items.name: simplex-noise
items.note: Seeded noise for terrain, weather and anything that should look made rather than random.

items.name: ink
items.note: The branching story language behind 80 Days, with a JavaScript runtime for dialogue and choices.

items.name: Kenney Game Assets All-in-1
items.note: Every Kenney pack in one download: 150+ 2D sets, 50+ 3D kits, UI, icons, fonts and 16 audio packs that all match. Cards, casino sounds and particles in Full House Run.

items.name: Complete KayKit Collection
items.note: Every KayKit set: adventurers with a shared animation rig, dungeons, hex tiles, city and board-game bits, as glTF ready for three.js.

items.name: Modern Interiors
items.note: Top-down pixel rooms in three sizes, with a character generator of outfits, hair and animations.

items.name: Modern Exteriors
items.note: Streets, shops, parks and vehicles that match Modern Interiors, for a whole town.

items.name: Modern Office, Modern Farm and Modern User Interface
items.note: The rest of the Modern set: office rooms, farm crops and animals, and pixel menus with a portrait generator.

items.name: RPG Fantasy Battlers and Fungus Cave
items.note: Big animated battle monsters, and a glowing cave tileset with its own cast.

items.name: Tiny Swords
items.note: A little medieval army with the Enemy Pack: units, buildings, terrain and effects for strategy and defence games.

items.name: Pixel Adventure 2
items.note: Twenty animated platformer enemies, each with its own trick.

items.name: Pirate Bomb
items.note: A bomb-throwing platformer kit: a hero, five pirates that kick or swallow your bombs, objects and tiles.

items.name: Kings and Pigs
items.note: A hammer-swinging king against bomb-lobbing pigs, with cannons, boxes, doors, hearts and a full tile-set.

items.name: Ninja Adventure
items.note: A whole top-down RPG in one pack, with a Godot example project: characters, monsters, tiles, UI, music and sounds.

items.name: Sprout Lands premium
items.note: Soft farming tiles, animals and characters, for cozy games.

items.name: Complete UI Essential Pack
items.note: Pixel panels, buttons, bars and icons in flat, paper, wood, stone and metal themes, for menus and HUDs.

items.name: Sonniss GDC 2026 Game Audio Bundle
items.note: 347 professional recordings, 7.5 GB: card dealing, crowds, weapons, weather, creatures and UI. Searchable by name on our side.

items.name: Cozy UI Pack
items.note: Pastel cartoon dialogue boxes, cards and panels, applied as 9-slice borders.

items.name: ITHappy 3D models
items.note: Low-poly City Characters and the Interiors bundle: the crowds in Spotted 3D and Detective Zombie, the rooms in Next Door.

items.name: game-icons.net
items.note: Over four thousand game icons as SVG, in any colour you set.

items.name: Quaternius
items.note: Rigged, animated low-poly characters, creatures and props.

items.name: Poly Pizza
items.note: Search thousands of free low-poly models by what they are.

items.name: Lospec palettes
items.note: Tested small palettes, for giving a game one look instead of forty colours.

items.name: Mixamo
items.note: Auto-rigging and a library of motion-capture animations for 3D characters.

items.name: Aseprite
items.note: The pixel art and sprite animation editor we own. Opens LimeZu and Fantasy Battlers source files and exports sheets with frame data.

items.name: LDtk
items.note: A level editor that saves plain JSON, for handmade campaign levels next to generated ones.

items.name: Tiled
items.note: The long-standing tile map editor, with loaders for every engine.

items.name: Rive
items.note: Interactive vector animation with state machines, for characters and buttons that react.

items.name: Nano Banana
items.note: Gemini image editing and generation. Card art, sheet edits and anything with text in it.

items.name: Freesound
items.note: A searchable library of recorded sounds. Check each one's licence.

items.name: jsfxr
items.note: Make retro blips, jumps and hits in the browser in seconds.

items.name: ChipTone
items.note: A deeper sound effect generator from SFB Games, with envelopes and layering.

items.name: ElevenLabs sound effects
items.note: Describe a sound in words and get a take back, for the one effect no pack has.

items.name: Incompetech
items.note: Kevin MacLeod's music library, sorted by mood and tempo.

items.name: Ovani Sound
items.note: Game music packs built to loop and layer, with intensity versions of each track. The free Mixtape Vol. 1 has one track in each of ten genres.

items.name: Google Fonts
items.note: Open fonts to self-host, so a game never waits on another server for its words.

items.name: Fontshare
items.note: Free display and text faces from Indian Type Foundry, with a character a stock font lacks.

items.name: Space Grotesk
items.note: The house face in the Zen look.

items.name: Game UI Database
items.note: Screenshots of menus, HUDs and inventories from thousands of games, filterable by screen type.

items.name: Interface In Game
items.note: Game interfaces collected screen by screen, including video of how they move.

items.name: Game Accessibility Guidelines
items.note: A plain checklist of what stops people playing, sorted by how easy it is to fix.

items.name: Game Programming Patterns
items.note: Robert Nystrom's free book on game loops, state, commands and events.

items.name: Red Blob Games
items.note: Interactive explainers for hex grids, pathfinding and map generation.

items.name: Game Maker's Toolkit
items.note: Short videos on why a mechanic works, from a designer's point of view.

items.name: Juice it or lose it
items.note: The talk that shows the same breakout game going from dead to delightful with feedback alone.

items.name: Slay the Spire: metrics driven design
items.note: How the card pool was balanced from pick rates and win rates across every run.

items.name: Puzzmo
items.note: A daily puzzle site done carefully: one set a day, groups, streaks and leaderboards.

items.name: Telegram Mini Apps
items.note: Web games that open inside a group chat, with the chat's people already signed in.

items.name: Discord Embedded App SDK
items.note: Activities: a web game that a voice channel launches and plays together.

items.name: Reddit Devvit
items.note: Interactive posts, so a daily game can live inside a subreddit.

items.name: CrazyGames developers
items.note: A web portal with a large audience and an SDK for ads, accounts and saves.

items.name: Poki for developers
items.note: A web portal that picks games, tests them with real players and pays a revenue share.

items.name: itch.io
items.note: Upload a web build and it is playable in an hour. Good for jams and early players.

items.name: Newgrounds
items.note: The original web game community, still voting and still playing.

items.name: Web Push
items.note: Tell subscribers today's board is up, including on iPhone from the home screen.

items.name: Steamworks
items.note: Store pages, builds, achievements, leaderboards and cloud saves.

items.name: steamworks.js
items.note: Steam's API from Node and Electron, for shipping a web game to Steam.

items.name: Electron
items.note: A web game packaged as a desktop app. Vampire Survivors launched on Steam this way.

items.name: Tauri
items.note: A smaller desktop wrapper using the system webview, for games that want a light download.

items.name: SteamDB
items.note: Follower counts, sales and release dates, for seeing how comparable games did.

items.name: How To Market A Game
items.note: Chris Zukowski on wishlists, store pages and which genres sell on Steam.

items.name: GameDiscoverCo
items.note: A newsletter on how players actually find games, with the numbers.

items.name: Steam Next Fest
items.note: The demo festival that turns a store page into wishlists, three times a year.

items.name: Playwright
items.note: Drives a real browser, so every game is loaded, played and screenshotted before it counts as shipped.

items.name: Sentry
items.note: Errors from real players' phones, with the line that threw.

items.name: tally
items.note: Our analytics. One script tag, SQLite on the server, no cookies, a live dashboard.

items.name: Ten Midjourney photographs of cartridges, cut out with real alpha.
items.note: A cartridge outline is not something a rounded corner can fake, so the silhouette is computed: colour distance against a per-scanline ground model, forced convex, with a separate shadow test used only to trim inward.

items.name: Each label is the game running.
items.note: The ledger photographs every live game. That plate is printed into the photo window of the shell the game was dealt.

items.name: The sound is synthesised.
items.note: Web Audio, scheduled on the audio clock so the seat lands with the cart and the chord with the light.
